language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The form is for cakes and pastry boxes that need a date and a pickup time, not for the bread shelf where people choose items on the same day. The front page asks for a name, a phone number, and the day of the celebration. We leave a wide blank space for a second phone number because some customers are traveling or sharing arrangements with another family member. The paper is pale cream with dark blue print, and the writing lines are thick enough to use with a pencil. The staff checks the form before putting it in the order folder.

On Saturday morning, a customer named Rosa brought in a form for a small anniversary gathering and asked us to make the pickup instructions easier to read. She had written the date as October eighteenth but had not put the year beside it, so I asked whether she meant this year. She said yes and gave me the year. While I was checking the rest of the page, she ordered one lemon cake with a thin layer of raspberry filling and a dozen plain butter cookies. The cake should be eight inches across, and the message on top should be written in dark green icing. She said the message was still being discussed at home and she would call us with the exact wording by Tuesday afternoon.

The recipient line needs to say Mina, not Quentin, because Mina is collecting the order after work and Quentin will be out of town on the pickup date. Rosa explained that both names appeared on an older order and the shop had once sent a reminder to the wrong person. She asked us to use Mina as the only person authorized to collect the cake and cookies. The phone number beside Mina belongs to her and is the number we should call if the pickup time changes. Rosa said that Quentin may still call the bakery with a question, but he is not listed as a recipient, and we should not release the box to him. The form has a small recipient field, so I wrote Mina in the name space and added a note on the back for staff.

Rosa also asked whether we could keep the cake chilled until four thirty because Mina finishes work at four and the drive to the bakery usually takes about twenty minutes. I explained that we could hold it in the cooler, but the exact pickup time should still be written on the form. She chose four thirty and said Mina might arrive a few minutes early if traffic is light. The cookies will go into a separate paper sleeve so they do not touch the frosting in the cake box. Rosa wanted the sleeve placed inside the larger bag rather than taped to the outside. She also asked for one small candle but did not want a number printed on it because she planned to bring her own decoration.

Section two covers the kitchen notes and the allergy check. Rosa marked that no guest had a known nut allergy and asked us to use the usual clean tray for the cookies. She said the cake could be made in the same kitchen as other products that contain nuts and did not request a separate preparation area. The baker should still check the ingredient card for the raspberry filling before starting because the supplier had changed the label last month. We keep that check on the form even when a customer has not reported an allergy. The cake should have a smooth top with a narrow border around the edge and no fruit placed on top. The filling stays between the layers and should not be used to write the message.

When I read the instructions back, Rosa said, “That is right, and I will call Tuesday with the words for the cake.” She asked if the message could be added by phone or whether she needed to come back to the shop. I told her that a phone call was enough as long as we heard from her before the kitchen began decorating the cake. She wrote Tuesday afternoon beside the blank message line and asked me to leave enough room for about six words. If the wording was longer, we could call her before using a smaller script. Rosa did not give an alternate message, and we left that part of the form empty rather than guessing what she wanted.

The deposit box showed that she paid thirty dollars by card, and the remaining balance would be due at pickup. I circled the card receipt number on the customer copy and put the shop copy in the folder for October orders. The form also asks whether the customer wants a receipt by email. Rosa gave us an address with her name and asked for the receipt there, but said not to send the pickup reminder to that address because Mina should receive the reminder instead. I wrote Mina phone reminder in the contact notes and checked the box for a text message. The system will send that reminder on the morning of October eighteenth unless the pickup details change before then.

Before Rosa left, I checked that the form included the cake size, flavor, filling, cookie count, decoration note, pickup time, deposit, and recipient name. She looked over the copy and pointed out that the year had been written in the date field but was easy to miss, so I added a line beneath it without changing the date. She took the customer copy and said she would keep it with the invitation list at home. The shop copy remains in the October folder, and the kitchen will see it after the message wording is added. The cooler shelf assigned to this order is the lower rack near the back door, where the cake can stay level until Mina arrives."}]
